title: Collapse SLA Breach Periods by Status
prompt: Your support platform tracks ticket SLA status in two tables: `breached_days` (dates when at least one ticket was in breach) and `compliant_days` (dates when all tickets met SLA). Every day from 2024-01-01 through 2024-01-31 appears in exactly one table—no missing days. Collapse consecutive same-status days into range periods. Output columns `status` (either 'breached' or 'compliant'), `start_date`, and `end_date`. Order the result by `start_date` ascending. Use the date-minus-rownumber technique to identify islands.
schema_ddl: CREATE TABLE breached_days (breach_date DATE NOT NULL); CREATE TABLE compliant_days (comply_date DATE NOT NULL);

composite_moves: UNION two tables with state labels
ROW_NUMBER partitioned by state ordered by date
date minus rownumber cast to integer for island group
GROUP BY state and island group
MIN date as start, MAX date as end

hints: Combine both tables into one result set with a status label for each row.
Use ROW_NUMBER() partitioned by status and ordered by date to assign sequential integers within each status.
Subtract the row number from the date (cast to integer) to create an island group identifier—consecutive dates with the same status will produce the same group value.
answer_key:
WITH combined AS (
  SELECT 'breached' AS status, breach_date AS d
  FROM breached_days
  WHERE breach_date BETWEEN '2024-01-01' AND '2024-01-31'
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'compliant', comply_date
  FROM compliant_days
  WHERE comply_date BETWEEN '2024-01-01' AND '2024-01-31'
),
islands AS (
  SELECT
    status,
    d,
    d - (ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY status ORDER BY d))::INT AS grp
  FROM combined
)
SELECT
  status,
  MIN(d) AS start_date,
  MAX(d) AS end_date
FROM islands
GROUP BY status, grp
ORDER BY start_date;

_meta.scenario: a customer support tool tracking ticket SLA breaches and reassignments
